readout: Complementation fitness of a yeast strain depending on the human protein, by DMS-BarSeq; higher is more functional
assay_method: Functional complementation in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, in which the human protein must substitute for its essential yeast orthologue for cells to grow, read out by DMS-BarSeq on a randomly codon-mutagenised library. Per-variant scores were taken from the authors' MaveDB deposit, using a raw assay score set rather than the machine-learning imputed and refined ones.
remark: The sequence is UniProt P63279 exactly, 158 aa, and every label verifies against it. 1 wild-type-equivalent rows collapse to the single WT row at their mean. 3 rows have a label this format cannot express. This is the raw DMS-BarSeq score set. The deposit's machine-learning imputed and refined sets are not curated, imputed values being computed rather than measured, and for UBE2I the 'joint data' set is also skipped because it merges the two raw assays that are shipped separately here. The paper covers four proteins; SUMO1 and calmodulin are not enzymes and are outside the scope, so only UBE2I and TPK1 are taken from it. Genotypes carry 1 to 11 substitutions, joined with ':': {1: 734, 2: 1164, 3: 815, 4: 416, 5: 164, 6: 62, 7: 27, 8: 17, 9: 9, 10: 5, 11: 1}. 175 rows collapse into 158 duplicate groups, worst spread 0.0000.
